classification.text_en: The surah names the people of the event the companions of the elephant (ashab al-fil).

origin.note_en: The Quran does not describe the origin of the elephant.

purpose.note_en: The Quran does not state a purpose for the elephant.

nature.note_en: The Quran does not describe the elephant itself. It names it only in the title of the people.

abilities.note_en: The Quran does not describe abilities of the elephant.

limitations.note_en: The Quran does not describe limits of the elephant.

relationship_with_humans.text_en: The surah names the people of the event after the elephant: the companions of the elephant.

quranic_events.text_en: The Lord made their plan go astray, sent birds in flocks against them throwing stones of sijjil, and made them like eaten chaff.

chronological_position.note_en: The Quran gives no date for the event.

location.note_en: The surah does not name the place of the event.

misconceptions.text_en: Educational interpretation (not scripture): the surah names the elephant only in the title of the people and says nothing of the elephant's actions, so this profile describes none.

lessons.text_en: Educational interpretation (not scripture): the surah shows a plan brought to nothing by birds in flocks and stones, and it is read as a lesson on God's power over human schemes.

vocabulary.text_en: Words used: al-fil (the elephant), ashab al-fil (the companions of the elephant), tayran ababil (birds in flocks), sijjil, 'asf ma'kul (eaten chaff).
